raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 10 December 2025 in Urban Science Volume 9, Issue 12, Article 525 (Received 5 November 2025; Revised 30 November 2025; Accepted 4 December 2025; both publication date and volume/issue year are 2025).
raw_response.rationale: The full text (N = 655 households surveyed across 67 blocks in Bukavu, plus GIS/spatial analysis) reports one inferential test with a p-value—a negative correlation between physical distance from the city center and drinking water service coverage (r = −0.42, p < 0.05, PDF p. 11)—along with a bivariate correlation matrix among physical distance, collection time, informal market water price, and waterborne diseases (r = 0.963, 0.066, 0.124, 0.411, 0.582, −0.431 without p-values/SEs, Table 3, PDF pp. 14–15). None of these inferential estimates test a rule-type legal, tenure, administrative, tariff-structure, or regulatory exposure on a water service access outcome (distance from the city center is a spatial/physical predictor failing narrow Criterion 2, and disease correlations target health rather than service access under Criterion 4). Although the paper discusses land tenure insecurity, parallel titles, formal vs. informal neighborhoods, tenant bill-payment disconnections, and institutional fragmentation, every statistic on those legal/governance dimensions is purely descriptive (e.g., 29.74% lacking land titles, 68% on periphery and 74% in informal neighborhoods lacking formal titles, municipality access rates of 45%–75% in Table 2 without inferential contrasts), and the logistic regression mentioned in Section 2.3 (PDF p. 7) is never reported in the Results.
